title: run_container's --windows-cross forwarding is unreachable: dispatch exits on WIN_CROSS before the container branch can run
detail: Dispatch exits unconditionally when WIN_CROSS=1, so run_container (the only caller that could forward --windows-cross into the image) is never reached with that flag set. The container-leg probe the usage/spec advertise cannot be driven through ci-local.sh at all; only a manual docker run reaches it.
recommended_fix: Remove the dead forwarding line and document the manual `docker run ... tools/ci-local.sh --in-container --windows-cross` invocation, or reorder dispatch so the container branch handles --windows-cross.

title: --windows-cross + --mac/--native silently discards the native suite, contradicting the 'never silently redefined' guard
evidence:
+# Flag conflicts fail loudly — they are never silently redefined.
+if [ "$WIN_CROSS" -eq 1 ] && [ "$FAST" -eq 1 ]; then
...
+if [ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ] && [ "$NATIVE" -eq 1 ]; then
...
+if [ "$WIN_CROSS" -eq 1 ]; then
+  run_windows_cross
+  exit $?
+fi
detail: WIN_CROSS+NATIVE passes both guards, then the WIN_CROSS-first dispatch runs the cross probe and drops the requested native 8-gate suite. The spec's task list also promises 'conflicting flag pairs rejected with exit 2' — only two of the three conflicting pairs are covered.
recommended_fix: Add a WIN_CROSS+NATIVE guard that exits 2 (mirroring the other two checks), or document WIN_CROSS precedence explicitly instead of claiming loud rejection.

title: CI pipefail-mirror claim is not kept: gates run via `bash -c` children that never inherit pipefail
evidence:
+# The workflow's steps all run under bash (ci.yml: shell: bash) — mirror that
+# so set -o pipefail semantics match CI exactly.
+SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]
...
+set -uo pipefail
...
+    if bash -c "$cmd"; then
detail: SHELL affects only build-time RUN steps; the 8 gates execute at runtime via `bash -c "$cmd"` from a `set -uo pipefail` parent, and pipefail does not propagate to child bash (verified: child SHELLOPTS lacks pipefail; `false | true` yields 0). GH's shell: bash also implies errexit, set nowhere for gates.
recommended_fix: Run gates through `bash -o pipefail -c "$cmd"` (and decide on errexit) so the replica matches GH's `bash -eo pipefail` semantics, or soften the comment to what the code actually does.

title: usage() tells users 'use --in-container for the container's' toolchain, but on the host that flag only changes the success-message text
evidence:
+  tools/ci-local.sh --windows-cross # EXPERIMENTAL: compile-only windows cross-build
+                                    # (probes the LOCAL toolchain; use --in-container for the container's)
...
+      echo "   ✅ windows_amd64 cross-build succeeded → app-win.exe (in-container; the --rm container discards it)"
detail: With --in-container on the host, run_windows_cross still probes the HOST toolchain — IN_CONTAINER only selects the message branch. If a host build ever succeeded, the message would claim 'the --rm container discards it' while app-win.exe actually persists in the worktree.
recommended_fix: Make the in-container message conditional on a real container marker (e.g. /src/.docker sentinel set in the image), and state the actual docker run command for the container-leg probe.

title: Summary leg label says 'linux container' for any non-native run, including direct host invocations of --in-container
evidence:
+  if [ "$NATIVE" -eq 1 ]; then LEG="native (macOS)"; else LEG="linux container"; fi
...
+if [ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ]; then
+  run_gates "$([ "$FAST" -eq 1 ] && echo 2 || echo 8)"
+  exit $?
+fi
detail: A user following usage()'s --in-container advice from the host gets gates executed natively on the host but a summary claiming 'LOCAL CI SUMMARY — linux container —'. The leg label misreports where the gates actually ran.
recommended_fix: Select LEG from IN_CONTAINER as well: container when IN_CONTAINER=1, native when NATIVE=1, linux container only for the default docker path.
